Classical borrowed-workspace and cancellation methods have substantial prior
literature; PR673 and PR689 preserve their relevant Bennett/catalytic-space
and related ladder attributions. Their complete notices remain applicable.
This package makes a scoped minimum/count claim for an explicitly defined
tree family, not a new general reversible-computation theorem.

Nearby pending #665 (spectral residual splitting), #677 (native DATA-shear
boundaries), and #679 (selector-volume batching) concern different interfaces.
None supplies executable code to this package. PR673's full-transform negative
result is explicitly retained rather than silently reopened by a lower local
leaf count.

**FanPUYen, concurrent PR714**, inspected at
`efad8a40094ab453c0525efef0b0eff2a5d8b850`, improves the root split when one
array is genuinely clean, while retaining balanced binary dirty children.
Our entire pool is arbitrary dirty input; we change the whole tree's arities
and partitions without a clean-array premise. The interfaces and optimization
domains differ. No PR714 implementation or claimed optimum is consumed.

**Sagar Thakrar / thakrarsagar, concurrent PR730**, at
`d222e348179cc02a54d6d26dbd2838944f62c6e5`, published an exact interval
optimizer for unbalanced contiguous binary/ternary echo trees and unequal

and pinned separately. The comparison runs that actual optimizer and its
literal words. The strict additional gain here comes from higher arities:
at 15 factors / five arrays, 160 becomes 152 through a four-child node.

**Ali Romman, concurrent PR744**, at
